title: CUET Mass Media Test 8
subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Mass Media - 318.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Mass Media papers 2024, 2025 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: CBSE Mass Media Studies, Classes XI-XII (curriculum mirrored by the NTA syllabus)
Constitution of India, Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(2); Acts and Supreme Court judgments as cited
Official histories of All India Radio, Doordarshan and Indian cinema
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a case; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Why radio reaches so many people
questions.question: Radio reaches remote villages more easily than most media mainly because it is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Cheap and portable
Why: Radio sets are cheap, run on batteries and can be carried anywhere, and listeners need not be able to read.
Why not the others: (B) describes TV. (C) is false. (D) is false; radio needs no reading.
Key point: Radio is the most accessible mass medium.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: The same joke may be welcome at a party but offensive at a funeral. This shows the importance of the ____ in communication.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) context
Why: Context is the setting (place, occasion, relationship) that shapes how a message is understood.
Why not the others: (A) carries the message. (B) puts the idea into words. (C) is the response.
Key point: Meaning depends on where and when a message is sent.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Programme)
(A) Magazine programme
(B) Running commentary
(C) Countdown show
(D) Radio quiz

List-II (Feature)
(I) Listeners or contestants answer questions
(II) Songs are played in order of popularity
(III) Several short items are put together in one show
(IV) A live description of a match or event
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: A magazine programme combines several items (III). A running commentary describes an event live (IV). A countdown plays songs by rank (II), and a quiz asks questions (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps magazine and commentary. (B) swaps commentary and countdown. (C) swaps countdown and quiz.
Key point: Radio formats suit different purposes and audiences.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about headlines:
(A) Headlines usually use the present tense, even for past events.
(B) Words like "a" and "the" are often left out.
(C) A headline should be as long as possible.
(D) A headline must be supported by the story below it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. "Floods hit Assam" is in the present tense, drops "the", and must match the story.
Why not the others: (C) is false. Headlines are short, so that they can be read at a glance. Options (B) and (C) include (C), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: A headline is brief, lively and accurate.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: The name for the Hindi film industry
questions.question: The popular name for the Hindi film industry based in Mumbai is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Bollywood
Why: "Bollywood" joins Bombay and Hollywood.
Why not the others: (A) usually refers to Telugu or Bengali cinema. (B) is Tamil cinema. (D) is Malayalam cinema.
Key point: India has many film industries in many languages.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: A letter, an email and a text message are all forms of ____ communication.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) written
Why: All three use written words.
Why not the others: (B) is spoken. (C) uses no words. (D) uses images.
Key point: Written communication leaves a record.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Journalism that argues for a cause
questions.question: Journalism that openly takes a side and argues for a cause, such as protecting forests, is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Advocacy journalism
Why: Advocacy journalism presents facts in order to support a cause or point of view.
Why not the others: (A) aims to present all sides without taking one. (B) relies on scandal. (C) reports from within a military unit.
Key point: Advocacy journalism must still be accurate.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Vox pop
(B) Sound bite
(C) B-roll
(D) Live phono

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Short interviews with members of the public
(II) A reporter's live report given over the phone
(III) Supporting footage shown over narration
(IV) A short clip of someone speaking
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: A vox pop collects opinions from the public (I). A sound bite is a short clip of a speaker (IV). B-roll is supporting footage (III), and a live phono is a report by phone (II).
Why not the others: (B) swaps vox pop and sound bite. (C) swaps sound bite and B-roll. (D) swaps B-roll and live phono.
Key point: A TV news report is built from these parts.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Body)
(A) NBDSA
(B) BCCC
(C) TRAI
(D) PRGI

List-II (Role)
(I) Regulates telecom and broadcasting tariffs
(II) Hears complaints about non-news entertainment channels
(III) Registers newspapers and periodicals
(IV) Hears complaints against TV news channels
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: The News Broadcasting and Digital Standards Authority hears complaints about TV news (IV). The Broadcasting Content Complaints Council covers entertainment channels (II). TRAI regulates tariffs (I), and the Press Registrar General of India registers periodicals (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps NBDSA and BCCC. (B) swaps BCCC and TRAI. (D) swaps TRAI and PRGI.
Key point: Print, TV news and entertainment have different regulators.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: The meter that shows sound level
questions.question: The meter on a mixing desk that shows the level of the sound, so that it is neither too soft nor distorted, is the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) VU meter
Why: A VU (volume unit) meter shows the audio level so that the operator can keep it in the right range.
Why not the others: (A) measures speed. (B) measures frequency. (D) measures light for photography.
Key point: Watching levels keeps the sound clean.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps of preparing an interview-based story in the correct order:
(A) Research the person and the topic
(B) Write the story using checked quotes
(C) Conduct the interview
(D) Prepare a list of questions
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (D), (C), (B)
Why: The reporter researches first, prepares questions, conducts the interview, and then writes the story using checked quotes.
Why not the others: (B) prepares questions before research. (C) interviews before preparing questions. (D) writes before the interview.
Key point: Good interviews depend on preparation.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Function)
(A) Surveillance
(B) Correlation
(C) Transmission of culture
(D) Entertainment

List-II (Example)
(I) Passing values and traditions to the next generation
(II) Reporting a cyclone warning
(III) An editorial explaining what a new law means
(IV) A comedy show that helps people relax
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
Why: Surveillance means watching the environment and reporting news (II). Correlation means interpreting events (III). Transmission of culture passes on values (I), and entertainment helps people relax (IV).
Why not the others: (A) swaps surveillance and correlation. (B) swaps correlation and transmission. (C) swaps transmission and entertainment.
Key point: Lasswell named the first three functions; Wright added entertainment.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Reporting what is said in Parliament
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution protects the media when they publish a substantially true report of the proceedings of Parliament or a State Legislature?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Article 361A
Why: Article 361A protects the publication of substantially true reports of legislative proceedings, as long as they are not made with malice.
Why not the others: (B) protects life and personal liberty. (C) is the right to go to the Supreme Court. (D) deals with amending the Constitution.
Key point: The public has a right to know what its legislators say.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Formats of advertising on the internet
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type)
(A) Native advertising
(B) Display advertising
(C) Search advertising
(D) Influencer marketing

List-II (Feature)
(I) Banners and boxes with images on websites
(II) Popular creators promote a product to their followers
(III) Paid content made to look like the platform's own content
(IV) Advertisements shown alongside search results
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Native advertising blends into the platform (III). Display advertising uses banners (I). Search advertising appears with search results (IV), and influencer marketing uses creators (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps native and display. (C) swaps display and search. (D) swaps search and influencer marketing.
Key point: Online advertising takes many forms, some hard to tell from content.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) John Logie Baird demonstrates television
(B) Samuel Morse sends a telegraph message between two cities
(C) Telstar, an early communication satellite, is launched
(D) Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: Morse's telegraph line opened in 1844, and Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Baird demonstrated television in 1926, and Telstar was launched in 1962.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1876 before 1844. (C) puts 1926 before 1876. (D) puts 1962 before 1926.
Key point: Each invention made communication faster and wider.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question: A text message says, "Your bank account is blocked. Click this link to update your details." This kind of fraud is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Smishing
Why: Smishing is phishing by SMS: a fake text that tricks people into clicking a link or giving details.
Why not the others: (B) provokes people with offensive posts. (C) publishes private details. (D) breaks into systems directly.
Key point: Banks never ask for details through links in text messages.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: One story told across many platforms
questions.question: A story told across a film, a web series, a comic and a game, each adding new parts to it, is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Transmedia storytelling
Why: Transmedia storytelling spreads one story across many platforms, with each telling a different part.
Why not the others: (A) is copying. (B) is selecting news. (D) is having too much information.
Key point: Convergence makes transmedia storytelling possible.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Political advertisements on social media need no certification.
(B) The Election Commission's Model Code of Conduct applies to social media campaigning too.
(C) Citizens can report violations of the Model Code through the cVIGIL app.
(D) Social media can be used to spread misinformation during elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (C) and (D) only
Why: (B), (C) and (D) are correct. The Model Code covers online campaigning, cVIGIL lets citizens report violations, and misinformation is a known risk.
Why not the others: (A) is false. Political advertisements on social media must be pre-certified by the Media Certification and Monitoring Committee. Options (A), (C) and (D) include (A).
Key point: Election rules now extend to social media.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Advertising ordered to correct a false claim
questions.question: A company is ordered to run advertisements telling the public that an earlier claim about its product was false. These are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Corrective advertisements
Why: Corrective advertising removes a false impression created by earlier advertising.
Why not the others: (B) builds curiosity before a launch. (C) keeps a known brand in mind. (D) promotes the company's image.
Key point: Regulators can require corrective advertising.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Shortening a story from the end
questions.question: Because news is written in the inverted pyramid, an editor short of space can shorten a story by cutting it from the ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) bottom
Why: The least important facts come last, so the bottom can be cut without losing the main news.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) hold the most important information.
Key point: The inverted pyramid makes trimming quick and safe.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Technologies in the history of cinema
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Silent film
(B) Talkie
(C) Technicolor
(D) CGI

List-II (Meaning)
(I) A film with recorded sound matched to the picture
(II) A film with no recorded dialogue
(III) Images created by computer
(IV) An early process for making colour films
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: A silent film had no recorded dialogue (II). A talkie had synchronised sound (I). Technicolor was a colour process (IV), and CGI means computer-generated images (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps silent film and talkie. (C) swaps talkie and Technicolor. (D) swaps Technicolor and CGI.
Key point: Each new technology changed how films were made and seen.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question: Which body runs a fact-checking unit that checks claims about the central government's policies and schemes?
options: D) Central Board of Film Certification
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Press Information Bureau
Why: The PIB Fact Check unit, set up in 2019, checks claims about the central government.
Why not the others: (A) regulates press standards. (B) conducts elections. (D) certifies films.
Key point: Several bodies, official and independent, now fight fake news.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: A short alert that a news app sends to a user's phone screen when a big story breaks is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Push notification
Why: A push notification is sent to the phone even when the app is not open.
Why not the others: (A) is a small file stored by a website. (B) links pages. (C) groups posts by topic.
Key point: Push alerts have made news instant.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: What to avoid in a radio news script
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT suitable for a radio news script?
options: B) Naming the source before the statement
D) Long lists of names and figures
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Long lists of names and figures
Why: Listeners cannot hold long lists in their heads. Radio scripts give only the most important names and numbers.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) all help the listener.
Key point: Radio news must be easy to follow at one hearing.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Arrange the following stages of a new TV series in the correct order:
(A) The episodes are produced
(B) The channel telecasts the series
(C) A producer pitches the idea to a channel
(D) The channel commissions the series
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: The producer pitches, the channel commissions, the episodes are made, and then the series is telecast.
Why not the others: (A) commissions before the pitch. (B) produces before commissioning. (D) telecasts before producing.
Key point: A channel decides what to commission based on its audience.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: TV signals sent straight to homes by satellite
questions.question: A service that sends television signals by satellite straight to a small dish at each home, without a cable operator, is called ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) DTH
Why: DTH (direct-to-home) delivers channels by satellite to a home dish.
Why not the others: (A) uses the internet. (B) uses ground transmitters. (D) uses a cable operator's network.
Key point: DTH reaches remote areas without cables.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A paper that comes out once a week
questions.question: A newspaper that is published once every week is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Weekly
Why: A weekly comes out once a week.
Why not the others: (A) comes out every day. (C) once a month. (D) once in three months.
Key point: Papers are classed by how often they are published.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Berlo's SMCR model names four elements. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Noise
Why: SMCR stands for Source, Message, Channel and Receiver. Berlo did not include noise, which came from Shannon and Weaver.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are three of the four SMCR elements.
Key point: Berlo focused on the qualities of each element, such as the source's skills.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: The end of the Vernacular Press Act
questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed by Lord Ripon in ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 1882
Why: Lord Ripon, the viceroy, repealed the Act in 1882.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are wrong dates. (D) is when the Act was passed.
Key point: The Act was resented because it targeted only Indian-language papers.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: One attempt at filming a shot
questions.question: Each attempt at filming a shot, such as the third try at an actor's line, is called a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) take
Why: A take is one continuous recording of a shot. The director may call for many takes.
Why not the others: (B) is a unit of action in one place and time. (C) is a roll of film. (D) is a group of scenes.
Key point: The editor chooses the best takes.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: An event that spread television in India
questions.question: Which event in 1982 led Doordarshan to start colour broadcasts and expand its network quickly?
options: A) The Commonwealth Games in Delhi
B) The Asian Games in Delhi
C) The cricket World Cup in India
D) The Olympic Games in Moscow
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The Asian Games in Delhi
Why: Delhi hosted the Asian Games (Asiad) in 1982. Doordarshan began colour telecasts and set up many transmitters for the event.
Why not the others: (A) were held in Delhi in 2010. (C) was first held in India in 1987. (D) were held in 1980.
Key point: Big events often push media technology forward.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: A platform built on photos and short videos
questions.question: Instagram is best known as a platform for sharing:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Photos and short videos
Why: Instagram is built around photos, short videos (reels) and stories.
Why not the others: (A) suits blogs. (B) suits professional networks. (C) suits wikis.
Key point: Visual platforms are popular with young users.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: What is not a kind of headline
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a kind of headline?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Dateline
Why: A dateline gives the place and date of a story. It is not a headline.
Why not the others: (A) runs across the page, (B) sits above the headline, and (C) heads the part of a story continued on another page.
Key point: Headlines come in several sizes and positions.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Children learn many of their society's values, roles and habits from the television and films they watch. This role of the media is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Socialisation
Why: Socialisation is the process by which people learn the values and norms of their society. The mass media are one of its agents.
Why not the others: (B) is reporting news about the environment. (C) is selecting news. (D) promotes products.
Key point: Family, school and the media all shape a child's values.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) An "A" certificate means the film is for adults only.
(B) A "U" certificate means the film can be shown to all.
(C) An "S" certificate is for specialised audiences, such as doctors.
(D) The CBFC also certifies newspapers before they are printed.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. The CBFC certifies films only; there is no pre-certification of newspapers.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (B), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Certification controls who may watch a film in public.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A short label for a story in the newsroom
questions.question: A one- or two-word label, such as "FLOOD-ASSAM", used inside the newsroom to identify a story while it is being prepared, is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Slug
Why: A slug is an internal label that tracks a story through editing. It is not printed.
Why not the others: (A) is printed above a headline. (B) names the writer. (D) is the paper's name at the top of page one.
Key point: Slugs help editors keep track of many stories.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Landmarks of Indian art cinema in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following films in the order of their release:
(A) Manthan
(B) Ankur
(C) Bhuvan Shome
(D) Pather Panchali
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D), (C), (B), (A)
Why: Pather Panchali came out in 1955 and Bhuvan Shome in 1969. Ankur followed in 1974, and Manthan in 1976.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1969 before 1955. (B) puts 1974 before 1969. (C) puts 1976 before 1974.
Key point: These films show the growth of realist and parallel cinema.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: In a conversation scene, the film cuts between one character speaking and the other listening, each seen over the other's shoulder. This technique is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Shot-reverse-shot
Why: Shot-reverse-shot alternates between two characters facing each other, which is standard for dialogue.
Why not the others: (A) cuts between two events in different places. (C) cuts in the middle of a movement to keep it flowing. (D) is a sequence of short shots that compresses time.
Key point: Shot-reverse-shot keeps viewers oriented in a conversation.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Community radio gives marginalised communities a voice.
(B) Mobile phones help farmers learn market prices before selling.
(C) Kisan Call Centres, started in 2004, give farm advice over the phone.
(D) Development communication uses only television.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Community radio is run by local people, phones bring market prices to farmers, and Kisan Call Centres give advice by phone.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Development communication uses every channel, from folk media and radio to phones and the internet. Options (B) and (D) include (D), and (A) leaves out (C).
Key point: The right channel is the one the community already uses.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Traditional media earned money mainly from advertising and subscriptions.
(B) In new media, anyone with an internet connection can publish.
(C) New media has no editors at all.
(D) News now spreads across platforms within minutes.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. News websites, apps and many platforms still employ editors and moderators.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (B), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: New media changed who can publish, not the need for editing.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Shortwave signals can travel very long distances by bouncing off the ionosphere.
(B) FM radio in India is broadcast between about 88 and 108 MHz.
(C) Medium-wave bands are used by AM stations.
(D) FM signals travel farther than shortwave signals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Shortwave bounces off the ionosphere, FM uses the 88–108 MHz band, and AM stations use medium wave.
Why not the others: (D) is false. FM travels in straight lines and covers only a local area; shortwave reaches across continents. Options (C) and (D) include (D), and (A) leaves out (B).
Key point: Wave band decides how far a radio signal travels.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: Who a children's channel is made for
questions.question: A cartoon channel plans its programmes and advertisements for children. Children are its:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Target audience
Why: The target audience is the group a channel or programme is made for.
Why not the others: (A) select content. (B) pay for programmes. (C) make programmes.
Key point: Every programme is planned for a target audience.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Community)
(A) Fandom
(B) Online support group
(C) Diaspora group
(D) Alumni group

List-II (Members)
(I) Former students of a school or college
(II) People living abroad who stay connected with home
(III) People facing the same health problem who help each other
(IV) Fans of a show, team or star
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: A fandom is made of fans (IV). An online support group helps people with the same problem (III). A diaspora group connects people living abroad (II), and an alumni group connects former students (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps fandom and support group. (B) swaps support group and diaspora. (D) swaps diaspora and alumni.
Key point: Social media helps build collective identities.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: The shape of a widescreen picture
questions.question: Most modern TV programmes are made in widescreen, with a frame that is 16 units wide for every 9 units high. This is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Aspect ratio
Why: The aspect ratio is the ratio of the frame's width to its height, such as 16:9 or the older 4:3.
Why not the others: (A) is frames per second. (C) is the number of pixels. (D) is how long the shutter stays open.
Key point: Widescreen replaced the older squarer 4:3 frame.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: A blog in which the creator posts videos instead of written posts is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Vlog
Why: A vlog (video blog) is a series of video posts.
Why not the others: (A) is audio. (C) is a jointly edited website. (D) is sent by email.
Key point: Vlogs are popular on video-sharing platforms.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: The officer who handles the media in a crisis
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

A customer in Pune finds a small piece of metal in a packet of "TasteMore" instant soup and posts a video online. Within hours it is shared thousands of times. When reporters call the company, its chief executive says only, "No comment." By the next morning, rumours claim that all TasteMore products are unsafe.

The company's public relations officer, Arjun, steps in. He advises the board to name a single spokesperson. That afternoon the company sends a statement to all newspapers and channels. It opens with the facts: two batches, identified by their batch numbers, are being recalled; customers should not eat soup from those batches and can return them to any shop for a full refund. The statement then explains what happened at the factory, gives a helpline number and apologises.

The next day the spokesperson holds a press conference and answers every question. The company posts daily updates on its website. An independent laboratory finds that the fault was limited to one machine, and the results are published in full. Three months later, TasteMore's sales are back to their earlier level.

Question: Arjun's role, in which he handles the company's relations with the media and the public, is that of the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Public relations officer
Why: The public relations officer (PRO) manages communication between an organisation, the media and the public, especially in a crisis.
Why not the others: (A) manages money. (B) runs the factory. (D) handles legal and board matters.
Key point: In a crisis, the PRO advises management on what to say and when.

An independent laboratory finds that the fault was limited to one machine, and the results are published in full. Three months later, TasteMore's sales are back to their earlier level.

Question: Why did the chief executive's "No comment" make the crisis worse?
options: A) Silence looked like hiding something, and rumours filled the gap
B) Reporters are not allowed to publish a "No comment"
C) It broke the rules of the Press Council of India
D) It forced the company to recall every one of its products at once
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Silence looked like hiding something, and rumours filled the gap
Why: When an organisation says nothing, people assume the worst. By the next morning rumours claimed that all products were unsafe.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are false. (D) did not happen; only two batches were recalled.
Key point: In a crisis, an information gap is quickly filled by rumour.

Question: The statement sent to the media opened with the batch numbers, the recall and what customers should do. This shows that a good press release:
options: A) Begins with the company's history
B) Keeps the main facts for the end
C) Opens with an apology before the facts
D) Puts the most important facts first
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Puts the most important facts first
Why: Like a news story, a press release follows the inverted pyramid: the key facts come first so that journalists and readers get them at once.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) bury the news. (C) is not what the case describes; the apology came later in the statement.
Key point: A press release is written the way a journalist would write the story.

Question: Why did Arjun advise naming a single spokesperson?
options: A) So that the company could avoid all questions
B) So that the company would speak with one consistent message
C) So that reporters would need a pass to ask questions
D) So that the chief executive could stay silent forever
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) So that the company would speak with one consistent message
Why: Different officials saying different things cause confusion and fresh rumours. One spokesperson keeps the message clear and consistent.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) go against the case, since the spokesperson answered every question. (C) is not mentioned.
Key point: One voice, repeated clearly, builds trust in a crisis.

Question: Which statement best explains why TasteMore's sales recovered?
options: A) The company spent heavily on new advertisements
B) The media lost interest and stopped reporting
C) The company changed its brand name after the crisis
D) It put safety first and shared the facts openly
questions.explanation:

Key point: Honesty and quick action are the heart of crisis management.
